sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Shri Rajeev Shrivastava and Shri Niraj Shrivastava, Ad
 petitioners.
 Shri Faisal Ali Shah, Advocate for the respondent.

Order 
1. Petitioner has preferred this criminal revision under Section 397/401 of Cr.P.C. being aggrieved by the impugned order dated 24.10.2024 passed by Principal Judge Family Court, Shivpuri in MJCR No.53/2024 whereby application under Section 125(1) of Cr.P.C. for interim maintenance has been dismissed.

2. Admitted facts of the case of petitioners are that marriage of Petitioner No.1 Smt. Saniya Khan has been solemnized with respondent Rizwan on 27.12.2020 according to the muslim culture and due to their wedlock, Petitioner No.2 was born.

3. Brief facts of the case of prosecution are that at the time of marriage of petitioner No.1 with respondent her father had given Rs.3,21,000/- cash and other articles as sufficient dowry as per demand of respondent and his NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20357 2 CRR-5861-2024 family members, but after the marriage, respondent and his parents started harassing the petitioner for non fulfilment of their demand of Rs.10 Lakhs as dowry.
They also demanded a plot for mother-in-law of petitioner No.1 and after getting the job, respondent thrown out petitioner from his house.
Thereafter, she was living with her parents alongwith petitioner No.2.

She has no independent source of income for maintaining herself and her son while respondent Smt. Saniya Khan vs Rizwan Ahamad Qureshi on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17291393/
1 being a Supervisor in T.B. Hospital, Shivpuri earning Rs.40,000/- per month.

sentences.text: Hence, petitioner has preferred an application for grant of interim maintenance of Rs.30,000/- for herself and her son and Rs.10,000/- as litigation expenses.

4. Respondent denied all these facts and submitted in his reply that petitioner No.1 pressurized him for living separately from his parents and on 7.11.2022, brother of petitioner No.1 took petitioner No.1 with him and said that her mother is going to Gwalior and she has to sit on the shop.
Thereafter, he went to her house for bringing her but on every occasion, she denied.
Petitioner No.1 lodged a false FIR against respondent and her family members under Sections 498A, 354A and 377 of IPC.
Respondent is a contractual employee and used to earn Rs.24,000/- per month.
His parents are also dependent upon him.
Therefore, he prays for dismissal of petition.

5. Trial Court after hearing both the parties considered that petitioner No.1 has sufficient independent source of income and she is running shop namely Sania Ladies Collection and she is also living separately from respondent without any sufficient source of income.
Hence, petitioner does not deserve for interim maintenance.
Being aggrieved by the aforesaid, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20357 3 CRR-5861-2024 petitioner has preferred this revision.
6. Learned counsel for petitioners contended that impugned order passed by trial Court is against law and facts and is without jurisdiction.
Petitioner No.1 has no independent source of income.
Petitioner No.2 is a minor child.
Therefore, it is duty of the father to maintain his child as per the same status.

Hence, he prays that impugned order be set aside and suitable order be passed in favour of petitioners for grant of maintenance of Rs.30,000/- for petitioner No.1 and Rs.10,000 for petitioner No.2 from the date of filing of this petition.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent opposes the prayer and prays for rejection by supporting the impugned order passed by trial Court.

8. Heard both the parties and perused the record.
9.
From perusal of record, it appears that since June, 2023 petitioner No.1 was living separately from respondent and respondent want to bring her to his house but she has denied.
Petitioner in his FIR categorically stated that she has passed Steno, B.Sc. and B.Ed. examination.
Therefore, it appears that she is highly qualified.
10. Counsel for respondent submits that petitioner No.1 Sania is running Shop namely, Sania Ladies Collection.
Photograph of shop was also produced before trial Court and petitioner did not file any affidavit to contradict the affidavit filed by respondent.
Therefore, prima facie, findings given by trial Court that petitioner No.1 is having sufficient financial source of income to maintain herself.
But, so far as petitioner No.2 is concerned, he is minor child aged about 2-3 years.
Therefore, it is clear that petitioner No.2 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20357 4 CRR-5861-2024 is not capable to maintain himself.
Respondent being father is duty bound to maintain his minor child.
Therefore, impugned order passed by trial Court in respect of Petitioner No.2 appears to be erroneous and deserves to be set aside.

sentences.text: Looking to the income of respondent and daily needs of Petitioner No.2, he is entitled to get interim maintenance of Rs.2,000/- per month from respondent.
12. In these circumstances, impugned order passed by trial Court is required to be modified.

Therefore, this criminal Revision is partly allowed and impugned order dated 24.10.2024 passed by trial Court is modified and it is directed that respondent shall pay interim maintenance to the tune of Rs.2000/- per month to Petitioner No.2 only.
13. With the aforesaid modification, this criminal revision is disposed of accordingly.
